summary: Tested Drug Browser Panel (Phase 1) - backend endpoint /api/drugs-db/browse-all and frontend sidebar UI on DrugsPage. All 6 requested features pass. Backend returns 292 drugs across 13 categories with expected counts. Frontend Browse All button opens sidebar, categories render with correct counts, expand reveals drug items with class/brand/effect count, search filters correctly (e.g., 'aspirin' -> 2 Hematological matches), and clicking a drug closes the sidebar. One notable React warning: duplicate keys for 'torsemide' and 'methotrexate' seen repeatedly in console (data-level duplication in categorized drugs list).

ui_bugs.issue: React 'Encountered two children with the same key' warnings for 'torsemide' and 'methotrexate' - duplicate drug ids appearing in categorized rendering. Likely present in multiple categories or duplicated in backend browse-all response.

action_items: Investigate duplicate drug ids (torsemide, methotrexate) in /api/drugs-db/browse-all payload or in DrugBrowserSidebar rendering. Ensure unique keys, e.g., prefix with category id or dedupe in backend.
critical_code_review_comments: Backend /api/drugs-db/browse-all appears to place same drug into multiple categories without ensuring unique React keys - main agent should either dedupe or make keys composite (categoryId + drugId).
Unrelated: repeated 'Stats fetch error: Failed to fetch' console errors on the drugs page - a stats API call is failing (likely blocked/CORS/wrong URL). Not in scope but worth cleaning.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Drug Browser Phase 1 verified end-to-end. NeuralNetworkVisualization.js and EnhancedBodyMap.js are not yet integrated - defer testing to Phase 2. Duplicate React key issue for 'torsemide' and 'methotrexate' remains open.
rca of the issue: Duplicate React key warnings occur because the sidebar renders drug items keyed only by drug id, while the same drug id appears in multiple categories returned by /api/drugs-db/browse-all. Fix by either (a) deduping in backend so each drug belongs to one category, or (b) using composite keys like `${categoryId}-${drug.id}` in the sidebar render.
